title: Hybrid segmented KV federation across tensor/pipeline boundaries for continuous batching
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: Continuous batching on production traffic exposes imbalanced KV cache pressure across heterogeneous multi-GPU deployments that use tensor parallel (TP) and pipeline parallel (PP) mixes. Small hot keysets (e.g., short dialogue prefixes) cause dramatic skew: some GPUs hold most hot KV slices while others remain underutilized but run forward/backward compute, increasing tail latency and wasting memory.

Goal: Introduce a hybrid segmented KV federation layer that slices KV state into hot/movable segments and fixed-owned slabs, coordinates placement across TP/PP boundaries, and provides low-latency prefetch + eviction semantics to preserve per-request latency SLOs while minimizing total GPU memory used. This must be compatible with existing KV RPC and multi-GPU runtimes and support safe fallbacks to single-owner semantics for compatibility and debugging.
acceptance_criteria: Unified placement API for marking segments as HOT or PERSISTENT; runtime uses new placement decisions during batch formation
End-to-end throughput overhead <= 6% compared to baseline while reducing peak GPU memory by >= 18% for skewed traces in our internal replay suite
Median extra token latency due to remote-prefetch <= 1ms; 99th percentile extra latency <= 8ms under production-like load

No correctness regressions: model outputs identical (bitwise deterministic) for requests that take identical model weights and prompt under the same parallel topology when fallback to single-owner is used
Can be toggled per-deployment via config flag and rolled out via canary on Dedicated clusters
design_notes:
High-level approach: split KV address space into small segments (~64-256KB) and classify each segment at runtime into three placement classes: LOCAL_OWNER (fixed owned by TP shard), HOT_REPLICATED (replicated to multiple GPUs for low-latency access), and MOVABLE_REMOTE (owned by a single GPU but eligible for on-demand prefetch).

Key ideas: continuous batching leverages request affinity vectors to predict near-future segment access; the federation coordinator uses a light-weight heuristic that combines per-segment hotness, GPU free memory, and pipeline stage locality to decide replication factor. For TP slices that are co-located with PP stage, we prefer LOCAL_OWNER to avoid cross-stage network hops. For pipeline boundaries where PP stages are on different hosts/GPUs, we favor HOT_REPLICATED with an LRU-like lease to keep replicated copies alive for a short time during bursts.

Memory accounting: we implement soft and hard quotas per-GPU for replicated segments; the coordinator runs an eviction plan every N seconds with gentle TTLs to avoid eviction storms. Prefetch uses a prioritized async queue ordered by batch-affinity score with a capped concurrency proportional to host NIC bandwidth.

Consistency: use eventual consistency for HOT_REPLICATED with write-through to the authoritative owner; during generation we pin authoritative slices to avoid stale reads for KV-write operations (e.g., cache warming writes). For inference-only workloads, reads from replicas are allowed without pinning to maximize throughput.

Telemetry: expose per-segment metrics (hotness, replica-count, last-access, prefetch-latency) and per-GPU memory utilization, and integrate with the Console rollout dashboard for per-route toggles.
decisions: Use small fixed segment size (default 128KB) to balance metadata overhead and granularity of replication
Lease-based replication (short TTL) preferred over indefinite replication to bound memory growth
Write-through to authoritative owner chosen to keep the protocol simple and avoid complex distributed consensus
Async prioritized prefetch rather than synchronous blocking fetch to avoid degrading tail latency for most requests
risks: Frequent churn of replicated segments could cause network pressure and eviction storms if prediction is poor
Edge cases where pipeline stages are on remote hosts may still see higher-than-expected latency for very long sequences
Debugging consistency issues is harder with eventual replica reads; need strong observability and an easy single-owner fallback
TP+PP topologies with very limited memory headroom may require conservative replication limits, which reduces benefit
testing_plan: Unit tests for segment allocator, lease manager, and prefetch queue
Integration tests in CI with a 4x-GPU multi-node TP+PP topology replaying skewed production traces (dialogue & searchworkloads)
Bench harness to measure median/99th latency delta and peak GPU memory under controlled skew (hot 10% of keys account for 70% of traffic)
Canary rollout on two Dedicated clusters with 10% traffic each, monitor Console metrics and circuit-breaker alerts
Chaos test: simulate transient network partitions and ensure coordinator gracefully degrades to single-owner reads
rollout_plan: Phase 1: library + unit tests in runtime branch feature/hybrid-kv-federation. Phase 2: internal nightly integration runs and perf tuning with trace replays. Phase 3: gated canary on dedicated-nyc and dedicated-ams with telemetry dashboards and alerting. Phase 4: expand to all Dedicated clusters and add Hosted API opt-in flag. Plan target: full rollout in runtime-1.22 minor release if metrics meet thresholds.

updates: 2025-11-15: Initial spike prototype that shards segments and implements lease metadata. Observed 22% memory reduction on skewed trace but 12% throughput regression due to synchronous fetches.
2025-12-02: Switched to async prioritized prefetch; throughput regression reduced to 3% in microbench; added soft quota and TTL eviction to cap replication.

2026-01-06: Integration run with 4-node TP+PP topology shows median per-token latency +0.7ms, 99th +6.5ms, peak memory down 20% in hot-skew scenario. Found a race in lease refresh causing occasional double-replication; fixed in PR 4278.

2026-01-24: Design review with Runtime and Platform leads. Agreed to expose config knob for replication aggressiveness and to default to conservative settings for Hosted clusters. Security requested a threat model doc for replica injection; assigned to Lauren Chen.

2026-02-03: Canary deployment scheduled for 2026-02-10 on two dedicated clusters. Monitoring thresholds and rollback criteria added to canary dashboard. Preparing PR for release notes and runtime-1.22 changelog.
